blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back once the Stripe account is closed) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (The nightly settlement worker can fail or not run without anyone seeing it) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back for the provider switch-over. When Paylane fails in production (outage, authorizations declined, capture errors) after the Stripe account is closed, redeploying the previous version brings back a Stripe client with no account behind it, and the next blue/green release is about a week away: card payments stay down. Keep the Stripe account open until Paylane has run in production for an agreed period, and either keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (the provider chosen from the environment) or state explicitly that the rollback is a redeploy of the previous version, valid as long as the Stripe account stays open. Add a task for the rollback path and for closing the Stripe account only after that period.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back once the Stripe account is closed

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Decide how an operator sees the worker fail. If the Paylane API is down at 02:00, the CronJob crashes or is never scheduled, nothing is reconciled and nothing alerts: the only alert the spec defines is for an unmatched payment, which a run that did not happen never raises. Have the worker log its start and end with structured fields (date settled, payments fetched, matched, unmatched), emit a metric or a last-success timestamp, and alert when a run fails or no successful run is recorded for the day; add this to the spec ("Payments are settled nightly") and to task 1.2.
findings.title: The nightly settlement worker can fail or not run without anyone seeing it
